layeringStrategies: Pair a soft attack instrument with one brighter transient layer if the melody needs definition.
Keep the support layer an octave above or below the lead when the main MIDI is sparse.
Avoid doubling every note with a wide stereo texture when the rhythm is already busy.
darkeningMoves: Low-pass the top layer slightly and shorten the release to keep the line moody.
Bias velocity toward softer hits so the melody feels more intimate than aggressive.
Use a mono or narrow lead and let width come from a quieter texture layer.
energyMoves: Shorter notes and higher velocity variance increase urgency.
Long tails, fewer notes, and lower registers reduce tension and feel more emotional.
Repetition with one accent change every bar makes a motif feel sticky without sounding random.
